A-DI-KI-TE-TE: PK Za 11 (GORILA 4, 32–4). Cf. Diqqiṯe “Diktu” (√d-q-q, Ugaritic dqt “female head of small cattle”); -TE-TE writes interdental /ṯ/ by doubling convention (cf. SA-SA = /š/). PK dialectal isogloss of JA-DI-KI-TU.
A-DU-RE-ZA: KH 11.1 (GORILA 3, 38–39; SigLA). Mis-transcribed by Davis: the tablet reads A-DU 𐄁 ZA, with a word divider; RE is absent. A-DU-RE-ZA is not an attested word.
A-DU-KU-MI-NA: ZA 10a.3–4 (GORILA 3, 168–71; SigLA). Unknown; cf. Ugaritic Ṯuka- muna (ṯkmn).
A-JA: SY Za 2 (GORILA 5, 64–5). Not in Davis’s appendix; cited in his body text formula table. Cf. Heb. ‫ ַחי‬ḥay “alive,” ‫“ יְ ִחי ַה ֶ͏מּ ֶלְך‬long live the king!” (1 Sam 10:24); Ar. ‫َ��ّ�ة‬ ḥayyah “serpent”; Heb. ‫ ַח͏וָּ ה‬Ḥawwāh “Eve” (Gen 3:20). Compare JA-JA /ḥayyā/ at PK Za 18 and SY Za 8 (√ḥ-y-y).
A-KU-MI-NA: ZA 10a.1–2 (GORILA 3, 168–71; SigLA). Unknown; apparently related to the preceding form, though the exact morphology remains unresolved.
A-MI-DA-O: PH(?) 31b.5 (GORILA 1, 318–19). Cf. Amorite PN type ʿAmmī-DN “My kinsman (knows)”; Šamšī-daʿi (Gelb AS 21, no. 6272), ʿAmmī-ṣaduqa (OB king, Gelb AS 21); Heb. ‫י͏שׁ ַ͏דּי‬ ַ ‫ ַ͏ﬠ ִ͏מּ‬ʿAmmīšadday (Num 1:12). Vowel variant of A-MI-DA-U (√ʿ-m-m + √y-d-ʿ).
A-MI-DA-U: ZA 10a.3 (GORILA 3, 168–71; SigLA). Cf. Amorite PN type “My kinsman knows” (Gelb AS 21). Vowel variant of A-MI-DA-O (√ʿ-m-m + √y-d-ʿ).
A-NA-NU-SI-JA-SE: HT Zb 159 (GORILA 4, 66; SigLA). Cf. base A-NA-NU (PN ʿAnānu, √ʿ-n-n) + -SI-JA-SE, the vessel-label adjectival formation (as on KI-TA-NA-SI-JA-SE, PE Zb 3). Alt.: ʿAnānu šī-yāṣē “ʿAnānu(’s)—which goes out” (disbursement clause).
A-NA-TI-*301-WA-JA: IO Za 8 (GORILA 5, 30–1). Fragmentary single-word inscription (broken edges both sides). ʿAnati nawaya (divine name Anat + nominal nawaya “dwelling”).
A-PA-RA-NE: HT 96a.1 (GORILA 1, 156–57; SigLA). Cf. Heb. ‫ ִ͏ﬠ ְב ָרנִ י‬ʿibrānī “Hebrew,” from √ʿ-b-r “to cross”; hence, “the crosser.”
A-RA-TU: ZA 7.1–2 (GORILA 3, 160–3; SigLA). Cf. Ug. ʾarṣ “earth,” Heb. ‫ ֶא ֶרץ‬ʾereṣ (√ʾ-r- ṣ).
A-RA-TU-ME: HT Wc 3024 (Hallager 1996, 34). Cf. Akk. erṣetum “earth” (fem. + mima- tion; √ʾ-r-ṣ).
A-RI-NI-TA: HT 25a.3 (GORILA 1, 44–5; SigLA). Cf. Heb. ‫ ֲא ִרי‬ʾarī “lion” (Gen 49:9); Ug. ary (KTU 1.5). PN paradigm with I-ZU-RI-NI-TA: “She-of-the-Lion” (√ʾ-r-y + -nīt).
A-SA-SA-RA-ME: IO Zb 10 (GORILA 5, 34), PK Za 11a–b (GORILA 4, 32–4). Davis’s PR Za 1c is a restoration (*802 for RA). Palaikastro preﬁx variant of JA-SA-SA-RA-ME (ʾa- for ya-); Heb. ‫ יָ ָ͏שׁר‬yāšār + adverbial -am (√y-š-r “be upright”).
A-SI-KI-RA: KH 20.2 (GORILA 3, 52–3; SigLA). Cf. Heb. ‫ ֵ͏שׁ ָכר‬šēkār “strong drink” + pros- thetic A- (√š-k-r).
A-TA-I-*301-DE-KA: ZA Zb 3.2 (GORILA 4, 112–13). If *301 = /na/, cf. tG √ʿ-n-y “who answered for you”; Heb. ‫ ָ͏ﬠנָ ה‬ʿānāh, Ug. ʿny; -DE-KA = dī-kā “for you” (relative dī + 2ms -kā).
A-TA-I-*301-WA-E: PK Za 11a (GORILA 4, 32–4). Cf. tG √n-w-y “dwell” (same paradigm as A-TA-I-*301-WA-JA).
A-TA-I-*301-WA-JA: IO Za 2.1 (GORILA 5, 18–9). Cf. tG √n-w-y “I make myself a dwelling”; t-stem shape as in Heb. hitnabbēʾ (√n-b-ʾ, 1 Sam 10:6).
A-TA-NA-TE: ZA 10a.2 (GORILA 3, 168–71; SigLA). Variant of A-TA-NA (ZA 9) with feminine -at- written -TE (ﬁnal vowel dead; √y-t-n “to give”).
DA-I-PI-TA: ZA 10a.4–5 (GORILA 3, 168–71; SigLA). Cf. LB da-i-pi-ta (KN Bk 799); pre- Greek, non-Semitic substrate PN attested in both scripts.
DA-KU-SE-NE: HT 103.4–5 (GORILA 1, 170–71; SigLA). Cf. Hurrian Daku-šenni (Nuzi/Ugarit); Hurr. tak- “to love” + -šenni “brother”—“beloved brother.”
DA-KU-SE-NE-TI: HT 104.1–2 (GORILA 1, 170–71; SigLA). Cf. Hurrian Daku-šenni (bare 2× on HT 103) + -TI, the ending on every entry of the HT 104 roster (DA-KU-SE-NE-TI, I-DU-TI, PA-DA-SU-TI, summed by KU-RO 95).
DA-MA-TE: KY Za 2 (Sakellarakis and Olivier 1994). Cf. Ug. dmt “tower” (DULAT 272), dmt-qdš “Tower of Holiness”; Akk. dimtu “tower-house” (√d-m-t).
DU-RE-ZA-SE: ZA 10a.5 (GORILA 3, 168–71; SigLA). Cf. DU-RE-ZA at Khania and Proto- Semitic terminative -s₁a: perhaps “toward Dureza” (Butts 2022, 539–58).
I-DA-MA-TE: AR Zf 1–2 (GORILA 4, 142, 162). Prothetic I- before DA-MA-TE (“the tower”; cf. KY Za 2).
I-KU-PA₃-NA-TU-NA-TE: AP Za 2.1 (GORILA 4, 4–5). Cf. Hurr./Anat. Kubaba: I- locative + kubānatu (the HT 47a/119 theophoric) + -NA-TE—either Sem. -na “our” + enclitic locative -te, or Hurr. =na (pl. article) + =ta/te (directive), “at/to the (our) Kubaba- attendants.”
I-NA-JA-PA-QA: PK Za 11d (GORILA 4, 32–4). Cf. Ar. ʾinna “behold” (√ʾ-n-n) + Heb. ‫ ָ͏פּ ַקח‬pāqaḥ “open (eyes)” (Isa 42:7); ḥ drops (√ʾ-n-n + √p-q-ḥ).
I-NA-JA-RE-TA: AP Za 2.2 (GORILA 4, 4–5). Cf. ʾina yirʾāta “in reverence” (√y-r-ʾ; Heb. ‫ יִ ְר ָאה‬yirʾāh “awe, reverence”).
I-PI-NA-MI-NA: PK Za 10 (GORILA 4, 29–31). Cf. Heb. ‫ ָ͏פּנִ ים‬pānīm “presence”; expanded form of I-PI-NA-MA (√p-n-y “face/presence”). The ﬁnal -NA invites comparison with Huehnergard’s reconstructed Proto-Semitic nonbound plural allomorph *-na af- ter long vowels (2019, 59–61).
I-TI-TI-KU-NI: HT 96a.1 (GORILA 1, 156–57; SigLA). Cf. Ug. √ntk “pour out” + energic -ni (cf. Amarna -ni, Heb. paragogic nun Job 19:2).
I-ZU-RI-NI-TA: PH 6.2 (GORILA 1, 292–93; SigLA). Cf. PS *ṯawr- “bull”; Ug. ṯr; Heb. ‫͏שׁ͏וֹר‬ šōr. Fem. of ZU-RI-NI-MA (√ṯ-w-r “bull” + -nīt).
JA-DI-KI-TE-TE: PK Za 15 (GORILA 4, 41). Cf. yā Diqqiṯe “O Dikte!” (vocative); -TE-TE = /ṯ/ by doubling convention. Same paradigm as JA-DI-KI-TU and A-DI-KI-TE-TE (√d-q-q).
JA-DI-KI-TU: IO Za 2.1 (GORILA 5, 18–9). Cf. Heb. yā Diqtu “O Dikte!” (vocative; to- ponym Dikte / √d-q-q).
JA-SA-SA-RA-MA-NA: KN Za 10 (GORILA 4, 8–9). Cf. Heb. ‫ יָ ָ͏שׁר‬yāšār “upright” + ‫ָמנָ ה‬ mānāh “to allot” (√y-š-r + √m-n-y).
JA-SA-SA-RA-ME: PS Za 2.2 (GORILA 4, 52–5; SigLA). Cf. Heb. ‫ יָ ָ͏שׁר‬yāšār “upright” + adverbial -am (√y-š-r).
JA-TA-I-*301-U-JA: AP Za 1 (GORILA 4, 2–3). Cf. tG √n-w-y (3ms preﬁx ya-; same paradigm as A-TA-I-*301-WA-JA).
KI-DA-RO: HT 117a.9 (GORILA 1, 196–99; SigLA). Cf. Heb. ‫ ְק ֵד ָרה‬qәdērāh “pot” (√q-d-r “earthenware”); Akk. diqāru “bowl” is the metathetic variant (q-d-r ~ d-q-r).
KI-TA-NA-SI-JA-SE: PE Zb 3 (Tsipopoulou and Hallager 1996, 31, 34–6). Cf. √k-t-n “linen”: kitāna (Ug. ktn, Akk. kitû, Aram. kittānā; Heb. ‫ ֻ͏כּ͏תֹּנֶ ת‬kuttōnet the garment derivative; χιτών via LB ki-to) + -SI-JA-SE, the vessel-label adjectival formation—“of linen, linen-ware”. Alt.: kitāna šī-yāṣē “linen which goes out” (disbursement clause).
KU-MI-NA-QE: HT Wc 3014a–b (GORILA 2, 76; SigLA). Cf. Heb. ‫ ַ͏כּ͏מֹּן‬kamōn, Akk. kamūnu, LB ku-mi-no (√k-m-n “cumin”). KU-MI-NA occupies side a; QE appears on side b before the CAP logogram and is likely from √q-b-b, cf. Heb. ‫ ַקב‬qab.
KU-PA₃-NA-TU: HT 47a.1–2 (GORILA 1, 90–1; SigLA), HT 119. Cf. Hurr./Anat. Kubaba + -ānu + -atu (feminine of KU-PA₃-NU).
KU-PA₃-NU: HT 1.3–4 (GORILA 1, 2–3; SigLA). Cf. Hurr./Anat. Kubaba + -ānu; rival Ug. Gupanu (√g-p-n). Seven tablets (HT 1, 3, 49a, 88, 117a, 122a, PH(?) 31a); on HT 88 it stands in one six-name roster with KU-PA₃-PA₃ (Kubaba herself).
MA-KA-I-SE: ZA 8.4 (GORILA 3, 164–65; SigLA). Cf. PS *mak(i)s- “customs ofﬁcial”; Heb. ‫ ֶמ ֶכס‬mekes (Num 31:28); Akk. miksu (√m-k-s, maqtil pattern).
MA-KA-I-TA: ZA 5b.2–3 (GORILA 3, 152–55; SigLA). Cf. Eg. mk.t “protection” (Egyptian contact).
NA-MA-MA-TI-TI-*319: HT Zd 155 (GORILA 4, 130–31; SigLA). Cf. Heb. ‫ נַ ֲ͏ﬠ ָמת‬naʿămāt “Naamath” (√n-ʿ-m “pleasant”); TI-TI writes /ṯ/ by doubling convention (cf. TE-TE = /ṯ/ on A-DI-KI-TE-TE). If *319 = /hū/: naʿmāṯ-hū “his pleasant one” (fem. + 3ms possessive).
PA-JA-RE: ZA 10b.5–6 (GORILA 3, 168–71; SigLA). Cf. Eg. pꜣ-y-Rʿ “He-of-Re” (Egyptian theophoric PN).
PA-RA-NE: HT 115a.4 (GORILA 1, 188–91; SigLA). Cf. A-PA-RA-NE above; shortened form.
RI-RU-MA: HT 118.4 (GORILA 1, 200–1; SigLA). Cf. Eg. rrj “pig” + mimation (Egyptian contact).
SI-KI-RA: HT 8a.4 (GORILA 1, 16–7; SigLA). Cf. Heb. ‫ ֵ͏שׁ ָכר‬šēkār, Akk. šikaru “beer” (√š- k-r).
SU-KI-RI-TA: PH Wa 32 (GORILA 2, 90; SigLA). Cf. LB su-ki-ri-to (KN As(2) 1516); to- ponym Sybrita (cross-script continuity).
SU-KI-RI-TE-I-JA: HT Zb 158 (GORILA 4, 64–5; SigLA). Cf. SU-KI-RI-TA + gentilic adjec- tive -TE-I-JA (toponym + gentilic).
TA-NA-I-*301-TI: PS Za 2.2 (GORILA 4, 52–5; SigLA). Cf. √ʿ-n-y “answer”: proposed N- stem 2fs preﬁx-conjugation, “may you answer,” with ﬁnal -TI interpreted as a t-based second-person feminine marker.
TA-NA-I-*301-U-TI-NU: IO Za 6 (GORILA 5, 24–7). Cf. √ʿ-n-y “answer”: N-stem 3fs jus- sive + 2ps object + energic -nū, “may she answer for you.” Sufﬁx-variant counterpart of TA-NA-I-*301-TI (PS Za 2) in the same formula slot.
TA-NA-TE: ZA 10a.1 (GORILA 3, 168–71; SigLA). Cf. LB ta-na-to (KN De 1618); possibly related to A-TA-NA-TE (theophoric PN, √y-t-n) or independently √ṯ-n-n (Tanit).
TI-TI-KU: HT 35.1 (GORILA 1, 66–7; SigLA). Cf. Heb. ‫ ִה ִ͏תּיכ͏וּ‬hittīkū “they disbursed” (2 Kgs 22:9); Ug. √ntk (KTU 1.14). Nun→geminate /tt/ (√n-t-k “pour out”).
U-NA-KA-NA-SI: KO Za 1c (GORILA 4, 18–20). hunna kanasī, “behold, my assembly!”: presentative hunna + √k-n-s + 1cs -ī (Heb. ‫ ָ͏כּנַ ס‬kānas “gather,” ‫ ְ͏כּנֶ ֶסת‬kәneset “assembly”).
U-NA-RU-KA-JA-SI: PK Za 12c (GORILA 4, 35–8). Davis prints U-NA-RU-KA-NA-JA-SI, but the published transcription reads U-NA-RU-KA-JA-SI amid damage. Cf. U-NA- RU-KA-NA-SI (IO Za 16) and U-NA-RU-KA-NA-TI (PK Za 11).
U-NA-RU-KA-NA-TI: PK Za 11b (GORILA 4, 32–4). Cf. hunna lu kanasiti; coda /s/ un- written, per the Linear B rule that drops syllable-ﬁnal s before a stop (Ventris and Chadwick 1956, 45; cf. pa-ka-na = phasgana).
U-TA-I-SE: KH 7b.2 (GORILA 3, 28–31; SigLA). Perhaps an onomastic form based on Amorite ʾūtaʾ/jūtaʾ “he found” (√w-t-ʾ; Gelb 1980), with ﬁnal -SE.
WI-JA-SU-MA-TI-TI-*319: HT Zd 157+156 (GORILA 4, 132–35). Cf. Heb. ‫ ָ͏שׁ ַמט‬šāmaṭ “re- lease” (√š-m-ṭ); TI-TI = /ṯ/ by doubling convention. If *319 = /hū/: šamāṯ-hū “his release” (fem. + 3ms possessive; Ug. -hu, Tropper UG §41.221.51).
ZU-RI-NI-MA: KN Zb 52 (Macdonald 2000, 64, ﬁg. 39). Cf. Ug. ṯr “bull”; masc. counter- part of I-ZU-RI-NI-TA + mimation (√ṯ-w-r “bull”).
*312-TA: HT 10b.2 (GORILA 1, 22–3; SigLA). Cf. *312 = KITNU (logogram); Heb. ‫ֻ͏כּ͏תֹּנֶ ת‬ kuttōnet “tunic, garment” (√k-t-n). The root is spelled out syllabically at PE Zb 3 (KI- TA-NA-SI-JA-SE).
*312-TE-TE: HT 26a.1 (GORILA 1, 46–7; SigLA). Cf. Ug. ktn “tunic, cloth item”; Heb. ‫ֻ͏כּ͏תֹּנֶ ת‬ kuttōnet “tunic.” If *312 = KITNU (logogram), TE-TE may represent /ṯ/ by doubling convention, yielding kitnūṯ, perhaps a linen or ﬁnished textile item.
